title: Phesgo maintenance

agents.name: Pertuzumab
agents.alias: Part of the combined Phesgo injection
agents.mechanism: Blocks HER2 pairing with other receptors
agents.explanation: Pertuzumab binds a different area of HER2 from trastuzumab. It limits receptor pairing, so the two antibodies act together at different points on the same growth pathway.
agents.watch: Keep echo appointments. Report diarrhoea, new breathlessness, swelling, palpitations or an injection reaction.

agents.name: Trastuzumab
agents.alias: Part of the combined Phesgo injection
agents.explanation: Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.
agents.watch: Keep echo appointments. Report diarrhoea, new breathlessness, swelling, palpitations or an injection reaction.

phases_note: After chemotherapy stops, use the agreed Phesgo maintenance plan (NCCP 00785 when eligible). Keep cardiac and response checks; chemotherapy steroids, antiemetics and growth factors do not automatically continue.
timeline_note: Treatment days show the planned pattern. Symptom bands are broad possibilities, not measured risk curves or a prediction of when you will feel unwell.
safety_note: Serious symptoms need assessment on any day, even if the chart shows a usual recovery period.
teachback: Which medicines are active now, when is your next echo or scan due, and who will review it?
consent_support: Discuss the aim, alternatives, uncertain benefit, common and serious risks, heart function, diarrhoea, injection reaction, fertility and pregnancy precautions. Effective contraception is required during Phesgo and for 7 months after the last dose; review the full combination and breastfeeding restrictions with the team. After chemotherapy stops, use the agreed Phesgo maintenance plan (NCCP 00785 when eligible). Keep cardiac and response checks; chemotherapy steroids, antiemetics and growth factors do not automatically continue.
urgent_extra: Contact oncology promptly for new breathlessness, swelling, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink or sudden illness. Tell staff immediately about rash, chest tightness or breathing difficulty during the injection.

support.title: Antiemetic plan
support.text: Phesgo alone has minimal emetic risk; routine prophylactic antiemetics are not populated.

support.title: Premedicines
support.text: No routine Phesgo premedication unless indicated by prior reaction or the individual plan.

support.title: Appointments and results
support.text: Echo before treatment and every 12 weeks (around cycle 5 if on time), including maintenance. Bloods before each cycle. Ask who books and reviews each test; report a missing appointment.

support.title: Phase transition
support.text: After chemotherapy stops, use the agreed Phesgo maintenance plan (NCCP 00785 when eligible). Keep cardiac and response checks; chemotherapy steroids, antiemetics and growth factors do not automatically continue.

questions.a: Phesgo is one combined injection of pertuzumab and trastuzumab under the skin of the thigh. It is not two separate injections and is never given into a vein.

questions.q: When is my next heart scan?
questions.a: Echo or MUGA before starting and every 12 weeks during treatment, including maintenance. At an uninterrupted 21-day schedule, the first 12-week check is around cycle 5; count elapsed time from the first HER2 dose. A delay or route/phase change does not restart the clock. Cardiac concern may require 4–8-week checks or urgent earlier assessment.

After chemotherapy stops, use the agreed Phesgo maintenance plan (NCCP 00785 when eligible). Keep cardiac and response checks; chemotherapy steroids, antiemetics and growth factors do not automatically continue.

Radiotherapy or surgery may be used for selected sites or symptoms. The teams decide timing and any pause in systemic therapy; there is no routine concurrent radiotherapy schedule in this NCCP regimen.

questions.q: Will I need CT scans, markers or DEXA?
questions.a: Baseline imaging records the disease sites. ESMO recommends response review generally every 2–4 months, adjusted for symptoms, disease pace, sites and treatment. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis is used when appropriate; the team selects the actual scan and review date. Tumour markers may supplement assessment, not replace scans or determine a treatment change alone. If hormone-receptor-positive disease leads to an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression, assess fracture risk and baseline DEXA when indicated. Repeat according to results, risk and the endocrine plan; DEXA is not a scan at each Phesgo cycle.

evidence.title: CLEOPATRA · metastatic dual HER2 strategy
evidence.intro: Evidence for the treatment strategy and for the SC formulation answer different questions.
evidence.population: Completed the chemotherapy component of dual HER2 treatment for metastatic or locally recurrent unresectable disease.
evidence.interpretation: CLEOPATRA evaluated IV dual HER2 blockade with docetaxel in metastatic disease. Continuing HER2 treatment after chemotherapy is part of the strategy; this is not a separate randomised Phesgo-maintenance survival comparison. FeDeriCa compared the combined subcutaneous formulation with IV pertuzumab plus trastuzumab in early breast cancer. It met the primary pharmacokinetic non-inferiority endpoint, with similar pathological response and safety findings. It was not a trial proving identical survival for every chemotherapy backbone or metastatic sequence.

chapters.title: The injection and your visit
chapters.intro: Phesgo is one combined injection of pertuzumab and trastuzumab under the skin of the thigh. It is not two separate injections and is never given into a vein.

items.title: Injection and observation
items.text: Loading/reloading 1200 mg/600 mg over 8 minutes with 30 minutes observation; maintenance 600 mg/600 mg over 5 minutes with 15 minutes observation. Alternate thighs; avoid sore, bruised or damaged skin.

items.title: Switching or a treatment gap
items.text: The team checks the last dual HER2 dose, including IV treatment: a gap of less than 6 weeks uses the maintenance dose; 6 weeks or longer needs reloading. A first Phesgo visit after IV treatment does not automatically require a loading dose.

chapters.title: Scans, heart checks and bloods
chapters.intro: Agree who books, reviews and acts on each result.

items.title: Blood tests
items.text: FBC, renal and liver profile before every cycle.

items.title: Heart ultrasound
items.text: Echo or MUGA before starting and every 12 weeks during treatment, including maintenance. At an uninterrupted 21-day schedule, the first 12-week check is around cycle 5; count elapsed time from the first HER2 dose. A delay or route/phase change does not restart the clock. Cardiac concern may require 4–8-week checks or urgent earlier assessment.

items.title: Longer-term cardiac plan
items.text: NCCP continues 12-week checks. ESC permits six-monthly echo only after the first year in selected asymptomatic low/moderate-risk metastatic patients with normal assessments, following an agreed specialist plan; moving to maintenance alone does not qualify.

items.title: Cancer imaging and markers
items.text: Baseline imaging records the disease sites. ESMO recommends response review generally every 2–4 months, adjusted for symptoms, disease pace, sites and treatment. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis is used when appropriate; the team selects the actual scan and review date. Tumour markers may supplement assessment, not replace scans or determine a treatment change alone.

chapters.title: Surgery, radiotherapy and hormone treatment
chapters.intro: Other treatment depends on your cancer and personal plan.

items.title: How surgery and radiation fit
items.text: Radiotherapy or surgery may be used for selected sites or symptoms. The teams decide timing and any pause in systemic therapy; there is no routine concurrent radiotherapy schedule in this NCCP regimen.

items.title: Endocrine treatment and bone health
items.text: If hormone-receptor-positive disease leads to an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression, assess fracture risk and baseline DEXA when indicated. Repeat according to results, risk and the endocrine plan; DEXA is not a scan at each Phesgo cycle.

items.title: Receptor and genomic tests
items.text: Hormone-receptor status can affect endocrine treatment. Oncotype-type chemotherapy triage is not applied to these HER2-positive regimens; treatment selection requires the appropriate indication-specific MDT assessment.

logistics.title: Your practical treatment plan
logistics.intro: Phesgo is one combined injection of pertuzumab and trastuzumab under the skin of the thigh. It is not two separate injections and is never given into a vein.

steps.title: Before the visit
steps.text: Confirm blood results, cardiac checks, active phase, previous dual HER2 dose and the consent discussion.

steps.title: The thigh injection
steps.text: Loading/reloading 1200 mg/600 mg over 8 minutes with 30 minutes observation; maintenance 600 mg/600 mg over 5 minutes with 15 minutes observation. Alternate thighs; avoid sore, bruised or damaged skin.

steps.title: No IV line for Phesgo itself
steps.text: Phesgo is given under the skin and does not itself require a port, cannula or take-home pump. Other treatment may still require access.

steps.title: Leaving the unit
steps.text: Confirm supportive medicines, next visits and due tests. Injection time is shorter than the whole appointment; preparation, assessment and observation still take time.

details.title: Switching / a missed appointment
details.text: The team checks the last dual HER2 dose, including IV treatment: a gap of less than 6 weeks uses the maintenance dose; 6 weeks or longer needs reloading. A first Phesgo visit after IV treatment does not automatically require a loading dose.

details.title: An existing port
details.text: Ask the line team whether the port is still needed and how it will be cared for or removed. Removal is a separate procedure; do not adjust the device yourself.
